headline: Iran-Oman deal close on Hormuz control, but strait remains closed; UAE reports ship attack
summary: While Iran and Oman near a deal on the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran insists the waterway won't fully reopen without US compensation, as the UAE reports another ship attack.
details: Iran and Oman are "very close" to an agreement regarding the administration of the Strait of Hormuz. However, Iran states that this deal alone will not be sufficient to fully reopen the strategic waterway.

The United Arab Emirates reported yesterday that Iran attacked one of its state oil company's carriers with a missile while it transited the Strait of Hormuz. No injuries were reported in this latest escalation of shipping attacks.

A US official indicated that Washington anticipates an agreement soon between Iran and Oman to resume normal oil traffic. Oman also described its negotiations with Iran as "positive and constructive."

This agreement is considered crucial for a broader resolution to the conflict that began with US and Israeli attacks on Iran on February 28. Iran's Foreign Minister stated that reopening the strait depends on additional conditions, including US compensation.

Tehran deems the previous shipping traffic separation scheme unacceptable and is discussing a temporary route with Oman. Technical and legal issues surrounding a permanent route are still being resolved.

Iran has responded to US attacks by targeting US bases in Gulf states and Jordan, as well as shipping in the narrow strait. Before the war, this waterway carried a fifth of the world’s oil and gas shipments.

Abu Dhabi National Oil Company reported that 15 of its vessels have been struck in "unprovoked attacks" since the conflict began, resulting in one crew member killed and 20 injured. Iran's Revolutionary Guards reiterated that reopening the strait depends on Washington accepting Iran's conditions and stopping interference.

A proposed deal would reportedly give Tehran control over ships entering the Gulf through the strait, a significant concession. US officials have previously insisted they would never agree to Iran controlling access to this vital energy trade route.
Iran has imposed tolls on oil tankers and fired on ships without permission, severely disrupting global shipments. This has caused energy prices to surge and fueled inflation worldwide.

headline_marked: [[Pirgachha police station besieged]] over JCD leader’s death in Savar
headline: Pirgachha police station besieged over JCD leader’s death in Savar
summary: Relatives and locals besieged Pirgachha Police Station in Rangpur, protesting the death of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi, who died after falling from a building during a police operation in Savar. They demand a fair investigation
details: Relatives and local residents besieged Pirgachha Police Station in Rangpur on Saturday, protesting the death of Chhatra Dal leader Monowarul Islam Bokshi. More than 200 people joined the demonstration, blocking the road in front of the station with Monowarul's body.

Monowarul Hossain Bakshi, 29, vice-president of the Savar unit of JCD, died early Friday. He fell from the rooftop of a residential building during a police operation at the Bangladesh Public Administration Training Centre (BPATC) Staff Quarters in Savar, Dhaka.

Officers from Pirgachha Police Station, assisted by Savar police, had raided Monowarul's father's flat at the BPATC Staff Quarters. The operation was reportedly to search for a missing teenage girl and her companion.

Protesters alleged police involvement in Monowarul's death and demanded a fair investigation and exemplary punishment for those responsible. Local political leaders intervened, bringing the situation under control.

Mofasirul Islam, member secretary of Pirgachha upazila JCD, called for a fair investigation to determine the cause of death and identify those involved. Aminul Islam Ranga, president of Pirgachha upazila BNP, stated that the autopsy and investigation reports would clarify the circumstances.

Mamdel Hossain Bokshi, the deceased's brother, alleged that the missing girl's father went to Savar with police, claiming one person accompanying them was in a police uniform. He said they were told to take Monowarul to the hospital quickly but could not save him.

Mamdel Hossain also stated they are preparing to file a case with Savar Model Police Station, demanding an impartial investigation and punishment for anyone found responsible, including police personnel. The officer-in-charge of Pirgachha Police Station advised relatives to file a case, assuring that actual circumstances would emerge through investigation.
